audit_notes: Model: through-thickness shear of the topcoat under a sliding contact with a time-averaged traction mu_avg*p, mu_avg = mu_gel*f_intact + mu_bare*(1-f_intact); u'' = 0, u(0) = 0, G u'(1)/t = mu_avg*p; metric: shear stress transmitted to the primer, G/t*u'(0) = mu_avg*p. Design: mu_avg = 0.05*0.8 + 0.4*0.2 = 0.12, tau = 24 kPa. Baseline (bare silicone, f_intact = 0): mu = 0.4, tau = 80 kPa. Gain 70 %, entirely set by the assumed friction coefficients and intact fraction (0.8), which is the untested self-healing claim. Chemistry check: seawater Ca2+ ~10 mM is enough to gel guluronate-rich alginate (gelation from ~1-2 mM), but Mg2+ (53 mM) and Na+ (470 mM) compete; Mg-alginate gels are weak, so the gel will be softer and more swollen than in freshwater Ca solutions; ionic crosslinks re-form in seconds, supporting the healing claim for the gel network but not for chains lost by abrasion (the brush must be covalently anchored). Fouling concern: diatom and bacterial EPS adhere to anionic surfaces through Ca2+ bridges, so this layer may increase slime adhesion; not simulated. Dimensionless: mu ratio 3.3, shear strain 0.073 (design) vs 0.24 (baseline). Simulation coefficient: mean traction 24 kPa (informational).
